title: Inspect and extend: Tabs as identifiable records
objective: Use the real implementation in `Sources/Models.swift` to demonstrate and safely improve browsertab identity, selected-tab behavior, close rules, and userdefaults persistence.
problem: A tab is a labelled bookmark to a current page. Follow its ID through selection and closing, then inspect what the store saves across launches and what happens when the last tab closes. Your implementation or debugging result must remain consistent with the source architecture.
requirements: Read `Sources/Models.swift` and the related project files: Sources/Models.swift; Sources/Screens/TabsView.swift; Tests/BrowserCoreTests.swift.
Add or improve a focused behavior related to browsertab identity, selected-tab behavior, close rules, and userdefaults persistence.
Add a meaningful unit test or, when platform tooling is unavailable, document a reproducible manual check.
Update documentation to identify local, simulated, external, and missing behavior accurately.
constraints: Do not claim or implement as complete a capability outside this boundary: Persisted URLs are ordinary browsing data and this sample has limited privacy guarantees.
Do not add credentials, personal records, real funds, or unsafe public network exposure.
Keep the change within the existing project architecture and name any new dependencies.
expected_behavior: A tab is a labelled bookmark to a current page. Follow its ID through selection and closing, then inspect what the store saves across launches and what happens when the last tab closes.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation change is traceable to `Sources/Models.swift`.
Normal and failure/edge cases are described and tested.
The test outcome and environment are recorded honestly.
README or source comments correctly state remaining limitations.
hints: Read the caller and the closest existing test before editing.
Separate a pure rule test from any UI, device, provider, or network test.
